title: The Sunday, learned
venue: Arthur's site (newspaper cadence: six dailies + a Sunday)
logline: Monday, week six. What a Sunday is: the strip draws Wood learning it — tiers, not panels; a page, not a row; watercolor he hasn't got. He buys a set. Cheap. The bad color begins.

panels.composition: The bedroom. WOOD with a library book: newspaper Sundays, a century of them. A tier layout traced onto the pad. BARNABY.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, a young man tracing a Sunday comic's tier layout onto a pad from a library book of old newspaper pages, a small dog

panels.composition: The pad: three tiers ruled. Beside it, a cheap watercolor set, eight pans, still shrink-wrapped.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, close-up of a ruled pad and an eight-pan watercolor set still in shrink-wrap

panels.composition: The wrap off. The first brush in water. The first wash on the top tier: too wet. Immediately too wet.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, a young man laying a watercolor wash across a ruled tier that is visibly too wet and pooling

panels.composition: The page, curling. The dog looking at it. Wood looking at it. The first bad color, on a Monday; Sunday's will be worse and the book keeps it.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, a young man and a small dog both looking at a watercolor page curling on a desk, no words

art.line: brush-pen scanned; muddy early-digital flats begin
art.palette: limited, muddy; Sundays in over-wet watercolor

notes: Tiers, not panels. The cheap set. Too wet at once.
